correctness.rationale: Proposition 2 uses \(A_\theta=1+(3-2q)\theta\), while Theorem 1 defines \(A_0=1+(3-2q)\). Reversing the theorem's own Lambert–Tsallis transformation shows that its output solves the CDF with \(A_0\), not the published CDF with \(A_\theta\). Subtracting those CDFs yields the exact nonzero residual for \(\theta\ne1\). Repeating the source's shift algebra with \(A_\theta\) gives the corrected formula and the exact real-domain condition \(\kappa_\theta=(3-2q)\{1-(q-1)\theta\}/(2-q)>0\). The packaged checker reproduces the formula numerically.

value.rationale: The quantile is advertised as a key closed-form property and is explicitly used to generate every Monte Carlo sample in the estimation study. All four simulation parameter designs have \(\theta\ne1\), and literal Eq. (9) produces substantial median CDF errors, including \(0.3787\ldots\) instead of \(0.5\) in one design. The correction therefore affects reproducible simulation, estimator benchmarking, and the claimed global analytical tractability of the model.
